# alta_router_config (Resource)

The configuration of one Alta router, written through the Alta cloud so the portal shows it.

Each section is optional. An omitted section is not managed; a present section is authoritative, so entries that exist in the portal but not in Terraform are removed. Every change is applied as one gated, commit-confirmed transaction: one push to the router, rolled back automatically unless health probes pass. Destroying this resource only removes it from state; it never erases the router's configuration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "alta_router_config" "route10" {
  site_id   = "aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTu"
  device_id = "0a1b2c3d4e5f"

  port_forwards = {
    game = {
      description = "Game server"
      protocols   = ["udp"]
      ip_version  = "ipv4"
      zone_in     = "wan"
      zone_out    = "lan"
      destination = { port = "8100" }
      translation = { address = "192.0.2.10", port = "8100" }
    }
  }

  vlans = {
    "3" = {
      name         = "IoT"
      router_ip    = "203.0.113.1/24"
      pool_size    = 243
      reserved_ips = 10
      domain_name  = "lan"
      dns_servers  = ["192.0.2.10", "192.0.2.1"]
    }
  }

  static_routes = {
    vpnret = {
      name     = "Return path"
      type     = "next-hop"
      network  = "198.18.20.0/28"
      next_hop = "192.0.2.10"
    }
  }

  switch_ports = {
    "2" = { tagged_vlans = [1, 2, 3] }
  }

  dhcp_reservations = {
    "02:00:00:aa:bb:cc" = "192.0.2.10"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `device_id` (String) Router device id: its MAC address, lowercase without separators.
- `site_id` (String) Alta site id.

### Optional

- `dhcp_reservations` (Map of String) Fixed addresses: lowercase, colon-separated MAC address to IP address.
- `firewall_rules` (Attributes List) Filter rules, in evaluation order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--firewall_rules))
- `port_forwards` (Attributes Map) Destination NAT rules, keyed by Alta rule id. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_forwards))
- `static_routes` (Attributes Map) Static routes, keyed by Alta route id. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--static_routes))
- `switch_ports` (Attributes Map) VLAN membership of physical ports, keyed by the portal's port index. Listed ports are managed; other ports and port settings such as speed or PoE are left alone. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--switch_ports))
- `vlans` (Attributes Map) Networks, keyed by VLAN id. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vlans))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<site_id>/<device_id>`.

<a id="nestedatt--firewall_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `firewall_rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) `ACCEPT`, `DROP` or `REJECT`.
- `id` (String) Alta rule id.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Name shown in the portal.
- `destination` (Attributes) Destination match. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--firewall_rules--destination))
- `icmp_types` (Set of String) ICMP types, for ICMP rules.
- `ip_version` (String) `ipv4`, `ipv6` or `any`.
- `limit` (String) Rate limit, e.g. `1000/sec`.
- `protocols` (Set of String) Protocols the rule matches; all when omitted.
- `source` (Attributes) Source match. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--firewall_rules--source))
- `zone_in` (String) Zone the traffic arrives from.
- `zone_out` (String) Zone the traffic is going to.

<a id="nestedatt--firewall_rules--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `firewall_rules.destination`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address or CIDR.
- `port` (String) Port or range, e.g. `443` or `50000-50100`.


<a id="nestedatt--firewall_rules--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `firewall_rules.source`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address or CIDR.
- `port` (String) Port or range, e.g. `443` or `50000-50100`.



<a id="nestedatt--port_forwards"></a>
### Nested Schema for `port_forwards`

Required:

- `protocols` (Set of String) Protocols to forward.
- `zone_in` (String) Zone the traffic arrives from, usually `wan`.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Name shown in the portal.
- `destination` (Attributes) Address and port the traffic is sent to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_forwards--destination))
- `ip_version` (String) `ipv4`, `ipv6` or `any`.
- `source` (Attributes) Restrict the forward to these sources. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_forwards--source))
- `translation` (Attributes) Internal address and port it is forwarded to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--port_forwards--translation))
- `zone_out` (String) Zone of the destination host.

<a id="nestedatt--port_forwards--destination"></a>
### Nested Schema for `port_forwards.destination`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address or CIDR.
- `port` (String) Port or range, e.g. `443` or `50000-50100`.


<a id="nestedatt--port_forwards--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `port_forwards.source`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address or CIDR.
- `port` (String) Port or range, e.g. `443` or `50000-50100`.


<a id="nestedatt--port_forwards--translation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `port_forwards.translation`

Optional:

- `address` (String) Address or CIDR.
- `port` (String) Port or range, e.g. `443` or `50000-50100`.



<a id="nestedatt--static_routes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `static_routes`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name shown in the portal. The portal refuses to save a route without one.
- `network` (String) Destination CIDR.
- `type` (String) `next-hop`, `interface` or `blackhole`.

Optional:

- `interface` (String) Outgoing interface.
- `metric` (Number) Route metric.
- `next_hop` (String) Gateway, for `next-hop` routes.


<a id="nestedatt--switch_ports"></a>
### Nested Schema for `switch_ports`

Optional:

- `all_vlans` (Boolean) Tag every VLAN on this port.
- `native_vlan` (Number) Untagged VLAN; the default VLAN when omitted.
- `tagged_vlans` (Set of Number) VLANs tagged on this port, when `all_vlans` is false.


<a id="nestedatt--vlans"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vlans`

Optional:

- `dhcp` (Boolean) Serve DHCP on this network.
- `dns_servers` (List of String) DNS servers handed out by DHCP, in order.
- `domain_name` (String) DHCP domain name.
- `isolation` (Boolean) Isolate clients from each other.
- `mdns` (Boolean) Repeat mDNS into this network.
- `name` (String) Name shown in the portal.
- `pool_size` (Number) DHCP pool size.
- `reserved_ips` (Number) Addresses at the start of the subnet kept out of the pool.
- `router_ip` (String) Router address and prefix, e.g. `203.0.113.1/24`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <site_id>/<device_id>. Import reads every section; drop the ones Terraform should not manage.
terraform import alta_router_config.route10 aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRsTu/0a1b2c3d4e5f
```
